runs.name: Sunbelt Rentals Holdings, Inc.
runs.entry: The operator's sheet lists the name as ASHTY, the former Ashtead Group plc ADR; Ashtead became a wholly owned subsidiary of Sunbelt Rentals Holdings, Inc. (Delaware) by a scheme of arrangement effective 2026-02-27, one SUNB share per Ashtead ordinary share, NYSE listing from 2026-03-02 (8-K 0001193125-26-085376); the run and this entry use SUNB; the done file carries ASHTY so the order file matches. Price **$75.17** (NYSE close 2026-10-09, aggregator, flagged) x **409,764,897 shares** (one class, 10-Q cover, 0001628280-26-061146; balance sheet 414,502,814 issued less 4,635,333 treasury at 2026-07-31) = cap **$30,802M**; sovereign **5.60%** (UST 30Y, 2026-10-09). Primary documents the FY2026 10-K (0001628280-26-044888, filed 2026-06-23), the Form 10 (10-12B/A 0001193125-26-050612) for Ashtead's US-GAAP FY2023-FY2025, and Ashtead's own IFRS annual reports 2021, 2022, 2023 and 2025 (ten-year histories in USD) for the long series, bridged for IFRS 16 and said so; FY2026 operating cash $3,784M cross-checked to the filed statement and XBRL. `tools/run.py` found no tagged history; every figure taken by hand. Lines of evidence derived by the analyst from the 10-K's Items 1, 1A and 7, as the overnight brief directs. Q1 IN (standard machines rented to about 800,000 US customers; the economics foreseeable in kind). **Q2 TOO HARD (NATURE)**: General Tool decides (61% to 70% of adjusted segment profit FY2024-FY2026); the filer's own words "the individual components of our General Tool fleet are similar to that of our peers"; a rival's 10-K (EquipmentShare) says "price is an important competitive factor"; EquipmentShare, founded 2015, built an $8.8B fleet and $4,379M revenue by 2025 at about 8% pre-tax on capital (the money test failed in volume); Sunbelt is number two (11% North American share against United Rentals' 15%) and not the low-cost operator (EBIT margin 19.6%, 22.4% adjusted, against URI 23% to 28% 2018-2025); the last deep construction cycle (Ashtead FY2003-FY2011) averaged about 9.5% pre-tax RoI with 4.6% at the trough, and URI's rental rates fell 11.8% in 2009; the better returns since FY2011 (14.5% to 19.4%) are not credited under Q2's change-for-the-better convention until a full cycle in which the field's price held. Re-look: the first fiscal year after FY2026 in which Sunbelt's North American equipment-rental revenue at constant currency, or URI's or the industry's, falls. General Tool adjusted segment profit -19% in two years ($2,394M to $1,932M) on rental revenue +3%. Integrity facts recorded, not judged: performance conditions on outstanding PSUs waived at the US listing and "deemed to have been met at 85.5% of maximum"; CEO pay $12.1M to $14.6M as operating income fell 13%; guidance; featured adjusted operating profit and adjusted EBITDA; a material weakness (a $550M note classed long-term when current) declared remediated. Q3 to Q12 not reached. Beneath the stop, COMPUTATION, NOT A CLEARANCE: maintenance-only owner cash (depreciation as the maintenance guess, specific e) all-equity FY2022-FY2026 average $1,804M, grown 3.31% a year; growth spending including acquisitions $1,436M a year, worth less than it cost, so the no-growth case is the top of the range; net debt $8,874M (operating leases $2,867M left out, said so). Range **$49.42-$56.94** all-equity (equity-only $57.48-$68.14); literal all-spending window, which changes sign, gives the no-growth case alone at $0.17 ($31.31 before acquisitions); expected return 4.46% to 5.89% on every case at $75.17, none near the floor; fair **$15.33** all-equity ($30.39 equity-only), not armed as an alert because the box is not OUT at Q7. Balance sheets FY2017-July 2026: fleet cost up 2.5 times FY2017-FY2026, net debt up 2.3 times April 2018-July 2026 to $8.5B; goodwill and intangibles about half of equity, tangible equity about $3.6B; receivables +13% in FY2026 on revenue +3%; fleet book value flat since April 2024 while average age rose from 49 to 53 months, so FY2026's cash came partly from not replacing equipment; FY2017-FY2022 balance sheets only partly available. Competitors on one plain pre-tax return on capital (the analyst's CONVENTION of this run): United Rentals 12.8% to 19.8% (2018-2025), Herc 4.2% to 14.0%, EquipmentShare about 8%, Sunbelt 14.5% to 19.2% (filer's RoI, FY2018-FY2025) and 14.4% FY2026 on the rivals' basis; Speedy Hire, HSS ProService and Vp flagged as not SEC filers. Contamination declared by the analyst: one filtered listing of `Test Runs/` for this company's names before the template copy, returning nothing; the session-start commit subjects (another company) and memory index lines; no blind-listed file opened. Commits one per question, last fbcf430d. Citations: the analyst's check 47 ids, 24 fragments, 0 problems; the dispatcher's script (`fold_cite_check.py`) 47 ids present, 24 fragments, 0 slips. Position note filled at the fold (not held). check_framework PASS. Analyst's gaps for the operator: (1) **the re-look event already happened**: FY2021 (US rental revenue -2%, the filer's dollar utilization 51% to 50%, URI fleet productivity -6.9%) meets the convention's literal trigger; the analyst judged it inconclusive, and another analyst could read FY2020-FY2024 as a full cycle, pass Q2 and close OUT at Q7 on price; the convention does not say whether the event must be a field downturn of a stated depth; (2) "the field's returns" has no defined measure; (3) specific (e) does not say which of two filer-given maintenance guesses to use when they differ (depreciation, or the filer's own $2.4bn replacement less used-equipment proceeds); (4) specifics (b) and (e) collide when the all-spending series changes sign; (5) the template does not say how a file closed before Q5 records integrity facts.
runs.narr: Listed as ASHTY on the operator's sheet; Ashtead redomiciled to Delaware as Sunbelt Rentals Holdings (NYSE: SUNB) on 2026-02-27. Q2 TOO HARD (NATURE): General Tool decides, an undifferentiated fleet by the filer's own words in a price-led field, a funded entrant (EquipmentShare) built an $8.8B fleet since 2015, Sunbelt is number two behind a lower-cost United Rentals, and the last deep construction cycle gave about 9.5% pre-tax returns and an 11.8% rate fall; the better returns since FY2011 wait for a full cycle in which the price holds. Beneath the stop, range $49.42-$56.94 all-equity and fair $15.33 against $75.17, no case near the floor. The analyst flags that FY2021 already met the re-look trigger, read as inconclusive; another reading passes Q2 and closes OUT at Q7 on price.
